definition: Two or more devices connected to share data
analogy: A road system moving cargo
example: Laptop and printer on home Wi-Fi
examTip: Includes wired and wireless; doesn't require the internet

definition: Very short-range network around one person
analogy: Whispering to the person next to you
example: Smartwatch paired to a phone over Bluetooth
examTip: Bluetooth = PAN. Smallest network type.

definition: Network covering one location, like a home or office
analogy: Hallways inside one house
example: Office Wi-Fi and Ethernet connecting every desk
examTip: Size order: PAN, LAN, CAN, MAN, WAN

definition: Connects devices within the same network
analogy: Hallways connecting rooms in a building
example: The box under a desk with many Ethernet cables
examTip: Works inside a LAN

definition: Connects different networks and directs traffic between them
analogy: The mailroom deciding where outgoing letters go
example: Home router sending LAN traffic to the internet
examTip: Routers connect networks; switches connect devices

definition: Converts the ISP's signal into data your network can use (modulator-demodulator)
analogy: Loading dock where the building meets the public road
example: The cable or fiber box from your ISP
examTip: Faces the ISP side; not the same as a router

definition: Lets wireless devices join a wired network
analogy: A doorway in from outside
example: Wi-Fi unit mounted on an office ceiling
examTip: Big part of Objective 2.3

definition: One network carrying voice, data and video as IP packets
analogy: One delivery truck carrying letters, packages and newspapers
example: Zoom calls and file downloads on the same office connection
examTip: Voice and video need QoS on converged networks

definition: Percentage of time a network or service is working
analogy: Percentage of hours a store is actually open
example: Status page showing 99.98% uptime this month
examTip: 100% isn't realistic; high availability is the goal

definition: 99.999% availability
analogy: A store closed only 5 minutes all year
example: Carrier-grade phone systems, critical data centers
examTip: About 5 minutes downtime per year. Four nines is about 53 minutes.

definition: Formal agreement defining expected service levels, like uptime
analogy: A written warranty promise
example: Cloud provider promising 99.99% uptime or service credits
examTip: The SLA is where the uptime target is officially stated

definition: A 7-layer reference model describing how data moves across a network
analogy: A floor map of a building that everyone uses to say where a problem is
example: "That's a Layer 1 issue" means check the cable
examTip: A model, not a protocol suite. Real networks run TCP/IP. Top down: All People Seem To Need Data Processing.

definition: The layer of raw signals over copper, fiber or radio
analogy: The road itself
example: A bad Ethernet cable or Wi-Fi interference
examTip: Cables, signals, hubs. Troubleshoot with cable testers and loopback tests.

definition: The layer for local device-to-device delivery using MAC addresses
analogy: A mail carrier delivering by name tag inside one building
example: A switch forwarding a frame to the right port
examTip: MAC addresses, frames, switches. The switching layer.

definition: The layer that moves data between networks using IP addresses
analogy: The full street address that gets a letter to another city
example: A router choosing the next hop toward Google
examTip: IP addresses, subnet masks, routers, fragmentation. The routing layer.

definition: The layer that gets data from one device to another and handles ports
analogy: The post office
example: HTTPS traffic using TCP port 443
examTip: TCP, UDP, port numbers. The post office layer.

definition: The layer that starts, manages and ends communication sessions
analogy: Dialing, holding and hanging up a phone call
example: A control protocol setting up a connection; tunneling
examTip: Start, stop, restart, control protocols, tunneling

definition: The layer that formats, encodes and encrypts or decrypts application data
analogy: A translator who also unlocks the lockbox
example: TLS decrypting HTTPS traffic so the page can display
examTip: SSL/TLS encryption and character encoding are Layer 6

definition: The layer of the network services users and apps interact with
analogy: The storefront customers see
example: A browser using HTTPS; DNS lookups; an FTP client
examTip: HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, DNS, POP3

definition: Media Access Control address, the hardware address of a network card
analogy: A name tag sewn onto a device
examTip: Layer 2. Not related to Apple Macs. Also called DLC address or EUI-48/EUI-64.

definition: Extended Unique Identifier, standard formats for hardware addresses (48-bit and 64-bit)
analogy: Short and long versions of a serial number
example: A typical Ethernet MAC address is EUI-48
examTip: Layer 2. Another name for MAC-style addresses.

definition: A Layer 4 protocol that delivers data between devices
analogy: Sending a package with tracking
example: HTTPS to a website over TCP 443
examTip: Layer 4. Details in 1.4.

definition: A Layer 4 protocol that delivers data between devices
analogy: Dropping a postcard in the mailbox
example: DNS lookups commonly use UDP
examTip: Layer 4. Details in 1.4.

definition: Splitting data into smaller pieces so it fits through a network, then reassembling it
analogy: Taking furniture apart to fit through a narrow door, then rebuilding it
example: A large packet split to cross a link that only allows smaller packets
examTip: IP fragmentation happens at Layer 3

definition: Protocols that encrypt data between apps (TLS is the modern replacement for SSL)
analogy: A lockbox only the two ends have keys to
example: The padlock icon on an HTTPS site
examTip: Layer 6 (Presentation) on the exam

definition: Each layer wrapping the data from the layer above with its own header
analogy: Russian nesting dolls, or letter, envelope, box, truck
example: App data inside TCP inside IP inside an Ethernet frame
examTip: Sender wraps going down; receiver unwraps going up

definition: The name for a chunk of data at a given layer
analogy: The same cargo called a package, pallet or container depending on where it is
example: Segment (L4), Packet (L3), Frame (L2), Bits (L1)
examTip: Some People Fear Birthdays: Segment, Packet, Frame, Bits

definition: A free protocol analyzer that captures traffic and decodes it by layer
analogy: An X-ray machine for network traffic
example: Filtering tcp.port == 443 to inspect HTTPS traffic
examTip: A protocol analyzer / packet capture tool (more in 5.5)

definition: Sending a signal out of a port and right back into it to confirm the hardware works
analogy: Talking into a microphone and hearing yourself through the speaker
example: A loopback plug on a network card or switch port
examTip: A Layer 1 troubleshooting technique
